goal: Consistent truth-based sorting and stable per-refresh discovery rotation across every VII public world and place slider.

intent_model.literal_request: Add sorting such as popular, lower price, higher price and top rated in every world, and randomize locations and places on every refresh across search and sliders.
intent_model.implied_outcome: Visitors can deliberately order results using meaningful data while the default discovery experience fairly rotates inventory on each new page load without flicker or loss of context.
likely_rejections: One world or slider family is missed.
Randomness causes cards to jump during interaction.
Unsupported or invented sort signals are exposed.
Sort state is lost on refresh or disagrees with the map.

interpretation_rules.operational_meaning: Inventory and cover all public result and place-slider families, not a representative sample.
interpretation_rules.acceptance_impact: A named cross-world matrix is required.

interpretation_rules.operational_meaning: Choose a new order for a genuinely new browser document and keep it fixed for the lifetime of that document.
interpretation_rules.acceptance_impact: Different seeds must rotate order; re-renders with the same seed must not.

cognitive_flow.current_layer: A compact 'sort by' control beside the result count and view controls.
cognitive_flow.current_decision: Choose the default refreshed discovery order or one supported explicit sort.
cognitive_flow.next_action: Browse or open a place from the now-ordered results.
deferred_complexity: World-specific filters remain in their existing panels.
Advanced ranking administration remains behind the management system.
preserved_depth: Map/list switching, filtering, availability eligibility, nearby recovery, progressive loading and URL sharing remain available.

natural_destination: VII public result pages and discovery sliders

facts.claim: Vacation and event search already expose partial sorting.
Discovery sliders already have a stable per-document seeded ordering primitive.

assumptions.claim: Popularity must only be offered when a verified review-count or equivalent signal exists.
assumptions.validation: Inspect each world data model and conditionally expose the option.

out_of_scope: Changing eligibility, availability or publication rules
Inventing prices, ratings, popularity or booking status
Accessibility and typography audits beyond preserving the current controls
invariants: Existing hard filters and availability exclusions remain authoritative.
Explicit price and rating sorts keep missing values last.
One document never reshuffles merely because state re-rendered.
Calendar, gallery and non-place semantic rails keep their intentional order.
affected_family: vacation search result routes and cards
event search result routes and cards
home, world and detail-page place sliders
Hebrew, English, Russian and French sort labels
list, grid and map result views

requirements.statement: Every public result world exposes a useful supported sort model.
Default results and place sliders rotate per fresh document but remain stable during interaction.
Explicit sorts persist in the URL and survive reload/back navigation.
Ordering never invents unsupported data or overrides eligibility and availability.
Map, list and progressive views share one ordered result set.

acceptance_checks.setup: Open each world with representative inventory.
acceptance_checks.action: Inspect and use every offered sort.
acceptance_checks.observable_result: The promised ordering is visible and unsupported options are absent.

acceptance_checks.setup: Open a result page and slider with at least four eligible items.
acceptance_checks.action: Re-render through filter/view changes, then perform a true browser refresh.
acceptance_checks.observable_result: Order is stable before refresh and rotates after a new document.
The URL and visible result order preserve the selection.

acceptance_checks.setup: Use inventory with missing price or rating values.
acceptance_checks.observable_result: Known values sort correctly, unknown values remain last and no value is fabricated.

acceptance_checks.setup: Choose an explicit sort then switch between list and map.
acceptance_checks.observable_result: The same eligible ordered set drives both views.

acceptance_checks.setup: A world has no verified numeric signal for an ordering option.
acceptance_checks.action: Open its sort control and exercise available options.
acceptance_checks.observable_result: The unsupported option is absent and the result family remains usable.

acceptance_checks.action: Record baseline and rollback identity before publication.
acceptance_checks.observable_result: The candidate can be rolled back without losing the last verified public version.

authorization_boundary: Implementation and candidate verification are authorized; production publication requires the exact candidate release gate and verified deployment route.
